How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is the exact REST‑style request you would send to the Cisco Nexus Dashboard API for the “get information of an interface” operation, using the parameters you supplied.

---

### 1️⃣ Full HTTP GET request (plain text)

```
GET https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed
Host: 192.120.45.67
Accept: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>   ←  (if your dashboard requires auth)
```

> **Explanation**  
> * `GET` – the HTTP verb for retrieving data.  
> * `https://192.120.45.67/...` – the base URL of the Nexus Dashboard instance.  
> * `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` – the endpoint that implements the “get information of an interface” API.  
> * Query string (`?fabricName=…`) – the parameters you listed, URL‑encoded.  

---

### 2️⃣ Equivalent function call (Python‑style)

If you’re calling the API from code that uses the helper function defined in the toolset, you can do:

```python
response = functions.requests_get({
    "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo",
    "params": {
        "fabricName": "Network1",
        "nodeId": 12,
        "podId": 10,
        "interfaceType": "Ethernet",
        "infoType": "Speed"
    }
})
print(response)   # <-- whatever the API returns
```

> **Note**  
> * The `requests_get` helper will automatically add the query parameters to the URL and perform the HTTP GET.  
> * If authentication is required, you’ll need to supply the appropriate headers or token inside the helper (not shown here).

---

### 3️⃣ Quick sanity check

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| `fabricName` | `Network1` | Limits the query to this fabric. |
| `nodeId` | `12` | Limits to node 12. |
| `podId` | `10` | Limits to pod 10. |
| `interfaceType` | `Ethernet` | Case‑sensitive; matches the enum `"ethernet"` in the API spec. |
| `infoType` | `Speed` | Requests speed information. |

---

That’s all you need to hit the API and retrieve the interface speed for node 12, pod 10, fabric “Network1”. If you run into authentication errors, double‑check that you’re passing a valid bearer token or basic auth credentials as required by your Nexus Dashboard deployment.
